positions.description: Developing software supporting the GMAS projects on the Emergent team. I served as lead dev on the Emergent team and 5th most senior classified dev on the project. To further support my colleagues I was also responsible for updating the guide for development in the classified environment and onboarding those new to it.

positions.title: Software Engineer Intern
positions.locationName: Albuquerque, New Mexico, United States · On-site
positions.description:
Responsibilities: Developed software supporting Air Force Research Laboratory science & technology
customers. Projects include:
•	WFOV Celestial Image Integration:  The Wide Field of View (WFOV) imaging system employed 25 staring cameras to image satellites in geostationary orbits. I designed and wrote software that aligns and integrates the sensor’s entire history into a “master image” in celestial coordinates. The primary complication was solving MATLAB’s memory inefficiency. After much experimentation I discovered that moving the code into for loops, even artificial ones, reduced overhead by at least 50%.
•	Multi-threaded AFSIM MS&A Framework:  I reduced simulation runtime by up to 80% through embarrassingly parallelizing AFSIM (Advanced Framework for Simulation integration and Modeling) batch simulation runs in Java.
•	Multi-threaded Directory Crawler:  A Java program that recorded a server’s contents at a point in time. Size, folder structure, file type etc. 7+ Tb is reduced to a 1 Gb snapshot for future analysis and monitoring.
•	Workstation Buildup:  Researched, designed, and built workstations for Tau’s Software Deployment Laboratory “SDL.”
•	Research:  Associated software like the Nasa Technology Transfer Program or VS Code for possible use by senior developers. Most of them now use VS Code in some capacity.
